description: Machine-readable source of truth for the EngineOS router. 32 entries for CLAUDE.md's 31 '| Intent (signals) | Load |' table rows — the +1 is the mobile store-release row split into ios-release/android-release intents — which stays the human mirror. scripts/validate-engineos.sh checks this file: C16 against CLAUDE.md (row count, drift alarm) and against registries/routing.json (every hook_mirrored intent carries a domain FK whose rules array matches the registry), and resolves every unqualified rule, skill and agent name to a file under rules/, skills/ and agents/; C18d checks suppression data integrity; C19 checks required_sections/required_fields/archive_contract (handoff, P4); C21 checks the record-change archive contract (P6). Plugin-qualified skill names (superpowers:*) and the external code-review skill are not resolved locally.

intents.title: New feature / multi-file change
intents.note: Resolve execution facts before artifacts. Eligible simple tasks ask a clickable Implement directly / Create a lightweight spec choice; direct needs only stack guidance and security/Git safeguards, with no mandatory prototype or PRD/ADR/tickets. Outside that exception >2 files or any new feature requires design. Accepted specs use Matt Pocock upstream-to-tickets for multiple bounded slices and a dependency graph; launch all independent ready workers within capacity. Tests and executable checks wait for entire implementation integration and fresh final user consent.

intents.title: Big / multi-domain / sweep work
intents.note: Both named rules are already always-on; the row names them to make the fan-out obligation explicit. Fan out via /engineos:implement <domain> <task> for changes, /engineos:audit for analysis, or N Task calls in ONE message over disjoint scopes. /engineos:implement dispatch is spec-gated. Tier is design: the row's primary work is fan-out planning and task decomposition, not the changes themselves.

intents.title: Bug / unexpected behavior
intents.note: Tier is design per registries/models.json work type hard-debugging.

intents.title: Backend work (NestJS)
intents.note: Application backends require NestJS, including API services, workers and LLM service hosts. Express/plain Node backend requests route to backend-coordinator for NestJS guidance; identify existing non-Nest backends truthfully and scope migration before extension. Express is allowed only as Nest's HTTP adapter. Node.js remains the runtime for tooling and libraries, not a backend framework choice. Rules follow routing.json; active frameworks are JavaScript/TypeScript only.

intents.title: Backend work (FastAPI)
intents.note: Inactive compatibility entry, retained until the next major release no earlier than one minor release after deprecation. No automatic routing; explain unsupported Python requests and ask for a supported Node.js stack.

intents.title: Frontend work
intents.note: Rules follow registries/routing.json's order (the registry wins); CLAUDE.md lists the same three with architecture first. Must be matched after mobile in the hook chain, since mobile screens are .tsx too. frontend-coordinator alias arturo.

intents.title: Mobile work / mirror web to mobile
intents.note: Store build/publish requests belong to ios-release / android-release, not here. Rules follow registries/routing.json's order (the registry wins); CLAUDE.md lists the same five with architecture first. All of them are adapted the mobile way: frontend.md for component/state patterns, backend.md for the API-consumption parts, observability.md as backend.md's closure target; react-patterns is adapted to React Native. mobile-coordinator (alias elias) covers greenfield mobile features and web->mobile mirroring, treats the web frontend as read-only reference when mirroring, and writes only in the mobile tree — never API/backend, web frontend, or DevOps.

intents.title: Mobile store release — Apple
intents.note: CLAUDE.md carries a single 'Mobile store release' row; it is modelled as two intents here so that each keeps a 1:1 domain FK into registries/routing.json, which has separate ios-release and android-release domains. Full pipeline: preflight, version bump, quality gates, signed build, TestFlight upload. App Store review submission and production rollout happen only on explicit instruction. Always-on security.md governs signing keys and store credentials. Precedes mobile in the hook chain by matching only build/release files, so ordinary React Native screens fall through.

intents.title: Mobile store release — Google Play
intents.note: Second half of CLAUDE.md's single 'Mobile store release' row, split to keep a 1:1 domain FK into registries/routing.json. Full pipeline: preflight, version bump, quality gates, signed AAB, track upload. Production-track rollout only on explicit instruction. Always-on security.md governs the upload keystore and Play service-account key.

intents.title: LLM/agent/chatbot work
intents.note: Last in the hook precedence chain. llm-coordinator alias hermsdorff. Active LLM/chatbot orchestration uses Mastra in NestJS backend providers; Node.js is the runtime. LangGraph/LangChain signals retain migration ownership, not active implementation defaults. Bare Mastra or chatbot requests and single agents do not require multi-agent topology approval. An LLM feature with no evals also matches the eval-setup row; defer eval authoring/execution until the approved final test phase. A system with more than one agent also matches the agent-system row, which owns the design gate.

intents.title: Multi-agent system design
intents.note: Interactive: llm-coordinator (hermsdorff) designs multi-agent Mastra workflows hosted in NestJS via patterns/3-Agent-topology-interview.md; developer approval recorded before workflow code. LangGraph signals retain legacy migration detection. Mastra/chatbot alone does not trigger this intent. The same signals trip decision rule rule-multi-agent-design, which folds the hitl reason topology-approval into resolve-task so the prompt advisor announces the gate; every phrase that rule's regexes accept is covered here or on the llm row, because the fold needs the floor an intent carries (src/kernel/resolve.test.ts holds the pair together). Spelled-out inflections (orchestrate/orchestration/orchestrator, multi agent/multiagent) because signals match as bounded literals, never as stems.

intents.title: DBA / data layer
intents.note: Rules follow registries/routing.json's order (the registry wins); CLAUDE.md lists architecture first. High floor: migrations are the canonical irreversible change. dba-coordinator (alias ronaldo) writes migrations and queries and holds NO database MCP; live schema and plan introspection is the read-only postgres-specialist / oracle-specialist leaves. routing.json names only dba-coordinator as the hook's agent — the two leaves are named by the CLAUDE.md row, so this array is a superset of the registry's single agent field.

intents.title: DevOps / infra
intents.note: High floor: infra config changes reach production by definition. devops-coordinator (alias hinokuma) writes config and holds NO cloud MCP; live cluster, cloud and CI introspection is the read-only kubernetes-specialist / gcp-specialist / cicd-specialist leaves. routing.json names only devops-coordinator as the hook's agent, so this array is a superset of the registry's single agent field.

intents.title: Editing security-sensitive files
intents.note: First in the hook precedence chain — cross-cutting, checked before every other domain, and delimiter-bounded so authors/ does not collide with auth/. security.md is already always-on; this row records a required security-reviewer pass (alias leo-ely), queued until final integrated scoped consent under rules/verification.md, which is design tier per registries/models.json work type adversarial-review.

intents.title: System comprehension / onboarding docs
intents.note: Docs and onboarding output only — defect and health findings go to the audit row. architecture-analyst (alias ricardo-fagmer) runs patterns/1-Analysis.md and produces code-grounded architecture and onboarding docs.

intents.title: Fill doc gaps by interview
intents.note: architecture-analyst in INTERVIEW mode (patterns/2-Interview-brainstorm.md). Interactive by design; folds the answers back into docs/. Not dispatchable non-interactively.

intents.title: End-to-end API QA
intents.note: qa-tester (alias ameer): clean-slate Docker up, endpoint inventory JSON plus Postman collection, headless Newman run of all endpoints and scenarios (skips MFA and email steps), pass/fail report. Dispatch only after implementation/integration and explicit current-task user approval; preserve configured non-interactive execution once approved.

intents.title: Multi-domain audit / system health check
intents.note: Read-only. Defect and health findings only; docs and onboarding output go to the system-comprehension row. The row names the command, not the agents: /engineos:audit <domain|all> fans out to the domain coordinators in AUDIT mode plus the read-only MCP leaf specialists, then consolidates via audit-consolidator (alias danilo) into a status report. agents is empty on purpose so this entry stays a faithful mirror of the table cell.

intents.title: Refactor / cleanup
intents.note: Finish with an explicit simplify pass over the diff: dead code, one-caller abstractions, and the hygiene rules of always-on base.md. Tier is design per registries/models.json work type hard-debugging, which covers cross-cutting refactor design.

intents.title: Architecture decision
intents.note: The decision gets recorded, not just chatted. Tier is most-capable per registries/models.json work type adr — an ADR is a recorded decision with a long half-life, the same class as a spec. Business, career and positioning decisions go to the strategy row instead; this row owns technical X-vs-Y choices.

intents.title: Release notes
intents.note: Stack-agnostic. Build tier rather than cheap: the notes are written against a real diff and a real version boundary, not summarized mechanically.

intents.title: Business / career strategy
signals: what do I learn, in what order
intents.note: Five modes over one grounding discipline: every claim traced to a dated web source or a file in this repo, output persisted to docs/strategy/. Technical X-vs-Y stays with the adr row. Tier is most-capable — the same problem-framing class as spec and PRD authoring in registries/models.json.

intents.title: Review / pre-merge
intents.note: The code-review skill is EXTERNAL — provided by the Claude Code environment, not this repo — so there is no skills/code-review/ directory and unqualified-name resolution must exempt it. It is listed unqualified because that is the name the router table and the Skill tool use. If the diff touches auth, input handling, data or LLM surfaces, also record the security-reviewer requirement and queue Agent-tool dispatch until final integrated scoped consent under rules/verification.md; that pass is design tier per registries/models.json work type adversarial-review, while the standards/spec review itself is the build-tier code-review work type.

intents.title: Test writing
intents.note: Hook-mirrored as the routing.json domain `test`, second in the hook precedence chain, so test files route here rather than to their stack domain. Dispatch test-writer (alias sameer) for well-scoped targets. Test authoring, suite execution and eval execution require explicit current-task user approval after implementation/integration is complete. Dispatch, configuration and environment flags do not authorize testing. Queue test-writer until ALL implementation tickets/corrections integrate and the user answers a fresh final clickable check prompt; earlier broad test requests are insufficient.

intents.title: Eval setup
intents.note: Scaffolding a harness against a known shape is build tier. Shares rules/llm-apps.md with the llm row, which this row will usually co-match. Test authoring, suite execution and eval execution require explicit current-task user approval after implementation/integration is complete. Dispatch, configuration and environment flags do not authorize testing.

intents.title: Independent verification of high-risk work
signals: release gate needs an independent pass
intents.note: critic (alias rogerio): adversarial correctness review, read-only, tries to refute the claim that the work is done. Required by rules/gates.md at risk=high; security-reviewer still owns the security lens. risk_floor high is the tier of the work under review — the row's own stated trigger — not of the review pass, which writes nothing. Tier design per registries/models.json work type adversarial-review.

intents.title: Handoff between agents, waves or sessions
intents.note: The row's load target is templates/handoff.md — a repo template, which is neither a rule nor a skill and so has no field of its own here. The section contract lives in required_sections/required_fields, validated against the template by scripts/validate-engineos.sh C19 — never restate the list here or anywhere else in prose except the CLAUDE.md row, which C19c checks. Never hand off with 'continue where you left off'. Cheap tier: the template is filled from state that already exists.

intents.title: Continuous improvement
intents.note: Mines .engineos/archived/, .engineos/skill-observations/log.md, eval failures and integrity failures for patterns with 3 or more occurrences, then proposes rule, skill and registry deltas as a PR. Proposes only; a human merges. Design tier because the output is policy change, not code.

intents.title: Skill/rule friction observed mid-task
intents.note: Continuous capture of skill and rule friction into .engineos/skill-observations/log.md, logged at the moment of friction. Capture only — the retro intent consumes OPEN entries and owns proposals and merges. Cheap tier: appending a structured entry to a log, no design work. Adapted from 'One Skill to Rule Them All' (CC BY 4.0, rebelytics.com).

intents.title: Work complete / close the change record

archive_contract.note: The change record is where delivered work claims conformance with its spec: spec: names the design-doc that rule-spec-threshold required, ## Verification carries the output-shown that rule-verification required, and the record itself is rule-change-record's artifact. Template checked by C21b, archived instances by C21c/C21d, prose mirrors by C21e. domains is deliberately NOT an FK to routing.json.domains — that enum routes file paths to hook domains (and has ios-release/android-release, no docs/general); this one files completed work. Records completed before grandfathered_before predate the schema and are never checked (archived/README.md: not migrated). instance_sections_since carries the P6 cutoff: the three evidence sections became scaffolded and required on 2026-08-06; earlier archived records legitimately lack them and the archive is read-only except for factual errors.

intents.note: Marks the record done, describes what was made, registers files changed and movements, and moves the record from .engineos/changes/ to .engineos/archived/. Clears the unrecorded-changes flag the Stop hook record-verify.sh enforces. The record schema is data in required_sections/required_fields/archive_contract, validated by scripts/validate-engineos.sh C21 — never restate it here, in .engineos/changes/README.md, or anywhere else in prose; _template.md is the one scaffold.

intents.title: Claiming done / complete / fixed; spec archived / feature shipped
intents.note: Evidence before assertion, always. For spec-archive and ship cases: all executable lint/typecheck/build/startup/tests/integrity checks require final integration and explicit current-task scope/revision approval, output shown, with a bounded fix loop — attempts, escalation and the never-repair floors per registries/policy.json repair, answered per attempt by scripts/kernel.sh repair; exhausting the bound reports red, never done. Automatic stop-verify.sh runs no checks and reports approval pending; record-verify.sh reports an unrecorded change record. Manual user-approved final checks supply Validation evidence, never Release permission.

intents.title: Ambiguous or multi-agent request needing a dispatch plan
intents.note: The router agent runs one scripts/kernel.sh resolve call FIRST and reasons only about the residue: intent tiebreaks the notes do not settle mechanically, scope decomposition against real files, and wave grouping. It returns a dispatch plan; it never dispatches and never edits. Tier is design per registries/models.json work type architecture, which covers task decomposition and fan-out planning. The deterministic path needs no agent at all — hooks/prompt-advisor.sh emits the kernel's answer directly when route-escalate reports escalate=false.
